Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. **Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).
## What

This change removes the duplicate file-system calls that caliper makes itself. tsrs is out of scope. Output is unchanged, so there is no changeset.

- **`Loader::resolution_scope` and `Loader::package_of`** walked every ancestor again for each directory they were asked about. They now memoise each directory they pass on the way up. The scope memo is single-flight (`Arc<OnceLock>` per directory, as `parsed` and `module_demands` do), because a load's demands all start together and racing threads probed the same directory up to 13 times. A wait only runs up the tree, so it cannot deadlock.
- **`ModuleResolvers`:** `types_first` is now `main.clone_with_options(..)`, so the two share one oxc_resolver file-system cache. Before, each made its own.
- **One `ModuleResolvers` per revision:** `Revision::build` and the lazy session's start build one set and pass it to both `dependency_types::load_with` and `ResolutionContext::with_module_resolvers`. Before, the loader and the context each built their own, so a run kept 4 oxc caches over the same `node_modules`.
- **`Loader::augmentation_scan`** passes the text it already read to `parse_source` instead of reading the file again.

Memory is bounded by the distinct paths touched. The scope and package memos hold one entry per directory passed, per load: 1305 probe paths on shadcn, and they are freed with the `Loader`. The shared oxc cache holds fewer entries than the four caches it replaces.

**Invariants and staleness:**

- The scope and package memos live inside one `Loader`, which means one `load` call, exactly as the per-directory memos they replace did.
- The shared resolvers live exactly as long as the context's resolvers did before. Watch revisions (`update_file` → `ResolutionContext::new_with_cached_ambient_global_files`), lazy updates (`Engine::new(.., ModuleResolvers::new(..))`) and lazy grows (`dependency_types::load`) still build fresh ones.
- No cache outlives a revision any longer than it did before. The one new sharing is between the load and the context of the same revision, which run milliseconds apart.

## Evidence

**File-system calls by caliper, excluding tsrs.** Counted with temporary instrumentation: a counting `oxc_resolver::FileSystem` plus counters at every `std::fs` site in `crates/core`. The instrumentation was removed before the commit. Command: `extract --quiet --load-dependencies --json`. The cached figure is the second run on a cache directory.

- shadcn: cold 84,578 → 40,116 (−53%); cached 65,118 → 28,050 (−57%)
- react-spectrum: cold 38,002 → 24,737 (−35%); cached 38,209 → 24,207
- chakra: cold 18,167 → 13,681 (−25%); cached 9,339 → 6,520
- antd: cold 17,688 → 11,304 (−36%); cached 14,733 → 8,864
- mantine: cold 12,161 → 7,739 (−36%); cached 11,674 → 7,101

**By call site on shadcn, cold (calls / distinct paths):**

- `resolution_scope` mark `exists()`: 28,628 / 1,305 → 1,305 / 1,305. The worst path was probed 1,340 times before.
- oxc `symlink_metadata`: 32,259 / 17,183 → 18,755 / 17,187
- oxc `read` (package.json): 3,546 / 1,584 → about 1,590 / 1,584
- `package_of` `is_file`: 1,950 / 693 → 769 / 693
- `Loader::read`: 1,656 / 1,382 → 1,646 / 1,382

**Output:** byte-identical JSON (parsed, `stats` dropped) between `extract --json --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies` built from origin/main 61ce2402 and this branch. Checked on all five corpora (shadcn, mantine, antd, react-spectrum, chakra), with the default collapse and with `--collapse-inherited-props none`: 10 of 10 identical, and no run had a non-info `SEMANTIC_BACKEND`.

**Wall time, CPU (user+sys) and peak RSS.** Medians of 5 interleaved runs against main, load 11.7-14.7. In each pair, main is on the left of the arrow and this branch on the right:

- shadcn: cold wall 1.19 → 1.10 s, CPU 5.66 → 5.44 s, sys 1.97 → 1.82 s, RSS 717 → 724 MiB; cached wall 0.63 → 0.59 s, CPU 2.31 → 2.12 s. A 9-run repeat at load 11: cold 0.98 → 0.94 s (sys 2.08 → 1.87 s), cached 0.54 → 0.52 s.
- react-spectrum: cold 0.60 → 0.56 s, CPU 3.26 → 3.17 s; cached 0.27 → 0.27 s, CPU 1.34 → 1.26 s
- chakra: cold 2.97 → 2.66 s, CPU 8.59 → 8.41 s; cached 0.92 → 0.90 s
- antd: cold 0.44 → 0.45 s; cached 0.11 → 0.10 s; CPU −2 to −4%
- mantine: cold 0.82 → 0.87 s in the 5-run batch, but 0.99 → 0.99 s in a 9-run repeat, so treat it as noise; cached 0.34 → 0.34 s
- Peak RSS is within ±1% on every corpus.

**Addon gates** (`gate_harness --tsc built-in`, gate-large, the binaries interleaved):

- first-answer, 3 rounds of 5: `firstAnswerMs` 129 / 132 / 131 on main and 130 / 129 / 129 on this branch. `startMs` 67 / 67 / 68 on main and 67 / 70 / 66 on this branch. Every run passed.
- memory: ok on both, `finalEqualsFresh`, peak arena 46 MiB on both.
- determinism: ok on both, the same bytes.

**Checks** (all exit 0):

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`
- `just test-checker-lane`, run outside the sandbox with no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 1719 passed. The 14 failures were the pty/watch tests (`watch_process`, `commands::*watch*`), which fail on "Operation not permitted" inside the sandbox. All 33 pass outside it.

**Tests that fail on base,** mutation-proved: putting back the base behaviour of all three changes made all four tests fail.

- `resolution_scope_probes_each_directory_once_per_load`
- `package_of_probes_each_directory_once_per_load`
- `concurrent_resolution_scopes_agree`, which asserts the 19 memo entries for 16 leaves
- `module_resolvers_share_one_file_system_cache`

The first two also assert that a fresh load sees the disk as it is now.

**The cached run:** cache validation is not what it spends. The DTS cache and the dependency index are one file each, and the package-stamp `metadata` calls total 782 on shadcn. What is left in a cached run is the checker, plus oxc resolution of the project's imports.

Independent check by the lead on head a1bf15e4 (a build of this head against a main-equivalent build, interleaved, release, `extract --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json`, load 13 to 20, runs with a non-info `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic dropped, none were): output (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) identical on mantine, chakra, shadcn and antd. react-spectrum differs only by the private-member rename of #512 (my main-equivalent binary predates it): after expanding the interned tables, 767 differences, every one a `name` `__#N@#type` to `#type`, 0 others. Medians main -> head (4 runs; shadcn repeated with 10): mantine wall 0.83 -> 0.86 s, CPU 3.13 -> 2.94 s, RSS 677 -> 642 MB; chakra 2.87 -> 2.63 s, CPU 9.66 -> 8.30 s, RSS 1191 -> 1067 MB; shadcn (10 runs) 0.99 -> 0.96 s, CPU 5.46 -> 5.28 s; antd 0.53 -> 0.51 s, CPU 1.82 -> 1.77 s; spectrum 0.71 -> 0.64 s, CPU 3.58 -> 3.29 s. A first 4-run shadcn batch read 1.28 -> 1.60 s at load 16 to 20, and did not repeat with 10 runs at load 13 to 15: load noise. The gain is modest (wall flat to a few percent, CPU 1 to 15% lower, RSS equal or lower), the fs-call reduction (25 to 57%) is the substantive result.

## Not verified

- The single-flight of the scope memo (as opposed to its memoisation) has no deterministic test. Replacing the `OnceLock` with get-then-insert only shows up as extra probes under a race.
- Sharing one `ModuleResolvers` between `load_with` and the context in `Revision::build` and the lazy session start is shown by the counts (oxc `symlink_metadata` 27.0k → 18.8k on shadcn). No test fails if either site goes back to `ModuleResolvers::new`.
- Timings ran at load 11-15, above the quiet threshold. They were interleaved, but the wall gains of 4-8% on shadcn and react-spectrum are close to the noise. The CPU and sys reductions held in every batch.
- I did not measure under `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`, and I did not run `just bench`.
- `test-napi`, `test-ts`, `test-integration`, `semver` and `deny` were not run locally (deny passed in the pre-commit hook).
- tsrs's own fs calls (realpath, read, exists) were not touched.
